entries.title: The intensity derivative uses closed pivotality
entries.locator: arXiv:1502.03050v3, Section 1.3, proof of Lemma 1.4, equation (1.8); the same formula appears in Section 1.5, equation (1.15).
entries.claim: The derivative sums rates times state-independent pivotal probabilities without the closed-edge factor.
entries.problem: For the single-bond event the derivative is $J e^{-\beta J}$, whereas the displayed formula gives $J$. Pivotality was defined independently of the bond state.
entries.correction: IENL gives $\frac{d}{d\beta}\mathbb P_\beta(A)=\sum_e J_e e^{-\beta J_e}\mathbb P_\beta(e\text{ pivotal})=\sum_eJ_e\mathbb P_\beta(e\text{ closed pivotal})$ for finite increasing events. FIXER derives the finite-set differential inequality by wiring the exterior to a sink and conditioning on the unexplored interior. This repairs the sharpness argument without differentiating an infinite-volume limit.
entries.leanImpact: When composing the product-coordinate Russo formula 71GK with the intensity parametrisation in IENL, retain the derivative of the bond-opening probability. A finite-set sharpness proof can then condition on the finite sink exploration and pass to the limit afterwards. It must not replace state-independent pivotality by closed pivotality without the closed-edge factor. The complete source PercLib/Percolation/Bond/WiredDerivativeFormula.lean and its collapse/unexplored-region dependencies at 22d8485da86b12aa41d1985b07939d2e6e612e26 now implement this finite-domain escape argument. The two-vertex appendix evaluates both escape as 1-exp(-beta) and its derivative as exp(-beta). This records implementation of the workaround, not author confirmation or a compiled correspondence review.

resolution.summary: Use closed pivotality, or retain the exponential factor for state-independent pivotality.
resolution.impact: The finite-set differential argument is repaired; the sharpness conclusion is retained.

entries.title: Critical field lower bounds require saturation
entries.locator: arXiv:1502.03050v3, Proposition 1.3 (printed p. 5) and Proposition 2.3 (p. 11); final conclusions of Sections 1.5 and 2.6.
entries.claim: The percolation and Ising magnetizations are bounded below by positive multiples of h^(1/2) and h^(1/3), respectively, for every h>0.
entries.problem: Both magnetizations are at most one, while these powers are unbounded. No fixed positive constant can make the stated global ranges hold.
entries.correction: Restrict to small fields or saturate the power at one. Under its explicit transitive summable-kernel and finite-critical-intensity hypotheses, 36PN proves $M(h)\geq\frac{1-e^{-1}}{2\sqrt2}\min\{\sqrt h,1\}$ for every h>0 by moment interpolation. For Ising, saturation would be $\min\{h^{1/3},1\}$; the separate Ising proof is not supplied by 36PN.
entries.leanImpact: 36PN is a percolation replacement only. A source wrapper must keep its hypotheses and field range. A bounded, nondecreasing magnetization extends a small-field power bound to a saturated global one; this observation does not establish the small-field Ising input or formalise that model.

resolution.summary: The saturated percolation lower bound is proved; the corresponding Ising proof is not supplied here.
resolution.impact: Restrict the field range or cap the power at one. This changes the global statement, while retaining its small-field form.
